title: Marche
quiz.0.question: Of the two Verdicchio DOCGs, which has more structure and greater ageing potential?
quiz.0.explanation: Verdicchio di Matelica lies in an inland valley at higher altitude with wide day–night swings, giving wines with higher acidity, more structure and greater ageing potential.
quiz.1.question: Which grape is the basis of Cònero DOCG / Rosso Cònero DOC?
quiz.1.explanation: Both Cònero DOCG and Rosso Cònero DOC are based on at least 85% Montepulciano, with a little Sangiovese allowed; most Cònero Riserva is 100% Montepulciano.
quiz.2.question: What aroma can Verdicchio Riserva develop with age?
quiz.2.explanation: Top Verdicchio Riserva can age 10–20 years, developing honey, nuts and petrol notes, similar to aged German Riesling.
quiz.3.question: What is the most striking feature of Lacrima di Morro d'Alba?
quiz.3.explanation: Lacrima di Morro d'Alba is one of Italy's most aromatic red grapes, famous for intense violet, rose and black cherry aromas.

slides.1.title: 🗺️ Central Italy's Hidden Gem
slides.1.content:
Marche lies on the east coast of central Italy, facing the Adriatic Sea, and is famous for the Verdicchio white grape and Montepulciano reds from Cònero.

Marche's wines are less famous than those of Tuscany or Piedmont, but their quality is excellent and their value outstanding.

slides.2.title: 🧭 Geography, Climate and the Industry (IWS Official Material)
slides.2.content:
⛰️
Topography
Mountains, hills and coast: the Central Apennines (including the Monti Sibillini) to the west, the region's emblematic gently rolling hills in the middle, and only a narrow strip of Adriatic coast to the east
🌊
Rivers
The Foglia, Metauro, Misa, Esino, Potenza, Chienti, Aso, Tronto and others run parallel to each other and perpendicular to the coast, from the mountains to the Adriatic, drawing sea air inland
🌡️
Climate
Mediterranean, with more continental influence towards the west; warmer south of Monte Cònero
🪨
Soils
Coast: sandy-gravelly marine sediments; centre: calcareous clay; inland: sandstone, marl and clay

slides.3.title: 🗺️ Marche DOCG & DOC Interactive Map
slides.4.title: 🍇 Verdicchio — Marche's Star
slides.4.content:
🌟 An underrated Italian white grape

Verdicchio ("little green one") is Marche's signature grape, able to make fresh, easy-drinking young wines as well as wines that develop complexity with age; it is genetically identical to Veneto's Trebbiano di Soave (Turbiana) — high in acidity, complex and age-worthy.

Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi DOC & Riserva DOCG

Location: around the town of Jesi

Size: Marche's largest appellation by area and production

Style: fresh, mineral, almond notes

Flavours: lemon, green apple, white flowers, almond, sea-salt minerality

Categories:

  • Classico Superiore (DOC): Classico sub-zone only, lower yields, higher alcohol, more structure
  • Riserva (DOCG, 2010): min. 18 months of ageing, often in wood

Verdicchio di Matelica DOC & Riserva DOCG

Location: the Matelica valley (inland, higher altitude)

Size: smaller, more boutique

Style: more structure, higher acidity, greater ageing potential

Flavours: white peach, lemon zest, almond, wet stone, herbs

Hallmark: high altitude and wide day–night swings → higher acidity, more concentrated flavour
slides.5.title: 📜 Castelli di Jesi and Matelica: The Rules Explained (IWS Official Material)
slides.5.content:
1950s-60s
Castelli di Jesi is the historic home of Verdicchio; Fazi Battaglia made Verdicchio hugely popular
1960s-80s
A shift from the traditional to the modern style in the 1960s–70s; mass production of simple, neutral wines in the 1970s–80s
1980s-90s
Quality producers rose in the 1980s; the press and wine critics took notice in the 1990s
2010
Riserva elevated to DOCG (Castelli di Jesi and Matelica)
🗺️ The Castelli di Jesi zone

Between the Adriatic and the Apennines, in the Misa and Esino river valleys; the Classico sub-zone roughly corresponds to the Esino valley and is bisected by the river, with key villages Montecarotto on the north bank and Cupramontana on the south.

⚪ Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi DOC

Same area and the same 99 MGAs as the Riserva DOCG, min. 85% Verdicchio (most are 100%). Four categories: the regular wine (fresh and simple, Marche's largest PDO by area and volume), Classico Superiore (Classico sub-zone only, lower yields, higher alcohol, more structured, complex and age-worthy, usually no wood), Passito and Spumante.

🏆 Castelli di Jesi Verdicchio Riserva DOCG

Stricter rules (lower max. yields, higher min. ABV), min. 18 months of ageing, often in wood; more structured, complex and age-worthy, and only a small share of Castelli di Jesi output.

⛰️ The Matelica zone

Much smaller than Castelli di Jesi and inland to its south-west, in Marche's only north–south valley; higher, cooler and with a wide diurnal range. The wines are less fruity and floral, more mineral, restrained and austere, and very age-worthy.

📋 Verdicchio di Matelica DOC & Riserva DOCG

Same area for both, min. 85% Verdicchio (most are 100%), 13 MGAs and no Classico sub-zone. The DOC covers still, Spumante and Passito, with no Superiore; the Riserva DOCG has stricter rules and min. 18 months of ageing — complex, structured and long-lived.
slides.6.title: 🍷 Rosso Conero & Rosso Piceno
slides.6.content:
Rosso Cònero DOC / Cònero Riserva DOCG

Conero Riserva DOCG

Location: around Monte Conero (Adriatic coast)

Grape: Montepulciano (85%+), Sangiovese allowed

Style: Rosso Cònero is lighter, fruit-forward and approachable; Cònero Riserva is dark, robust, full-bodied, tannic and high in alcohol

Flavours: black cherry, plum, spice, vanilla, leather

Hallmark: Montepulciano needs warmth to ripen fully, and it is warmer south of Cònero

Riserva: min. 2 years of ageing; most producers use 100% Montepulciano

Rosso Piceno DOC

DOC

Location: central-southern Marche

Grapes: Montepulciano (35–85%) + Sangiovese (15–50%); there is also Rosso Piceno Sangiovese (85–100% Sangiovese)

Style: medium-bodied, easy-drinking, fruity

Flavours: red cherry, berries, herbs, spice

Hallmark: Marche's everyday red, excellent value

Superiore: a sub-zone in the south-east corner, lower yields, higher alcohol, released no earlier than 1 November of the year after harvest
slides.7.title: 🏅 Cònero, Serrapetrona, Offida and Piceno Rules (IWS Official Material)
slides.7.content:
🏔️ Cònero Riserva DOCG & Rosso Cònero DOC

DOCG: min. 85% Montepulciano (max. 15% Sangiovese), most producers use 100% Montepulciano; min. 2 years of ageing; dark, robust, full-bodied, tannic and high in alcohol.

DOC: min. 85% Montepulciano; lighter, fruitier and more approachable. The zone surrounds the Monte Cònero promontory south of Ancona.

🌹 Lacrima di Morro d’Alba DOC

Min. 85% Lacrima, plus the richer, fuller-bodied Superiore and a Passito. Lacrima means "teardrop"; native to the area around Morro d’Alba, it gives deep purple wines with intense rose and violet aromas.

🍾 Vernaccia di Serrapetrona DOCG & Serrapetrona DOC

Both share the same area and require min. 85% Vernaccia Nera (most are 100%). Vernaccia Nera is a biotype of Cannonau (Grenache), unrelated to other Vernaccias and grown only around Serrapetrona.

DOCG: Italy's only DOCG that makes only red sparkling wine; at least 40% of the grapes must be dried (appassimento) and the wine undergoes three fermentations; secco or dolce. DOC: still, dry reds, sometimes from semi-dried grapes, min. 10 months of ageing.

🐑 Offida DOCG & Terre di Offida DOC

Offida Pecorino DOCG: min. 85% Pecorino; Offida Passerina DOCG: min. 85% Passerina (most are 100%); Offida Rosso DOCG: min. 85% Montepulciano (Cabernet Sauvignon allowed as a partner), min. 24 months of ageing (12 in wood, 3 in bottle), from a slightly smaller area.

Terre di Offida DOC: mostly Passerina, made in only three styles — spumante, passito and vino santo.

🫐 Rosso Piceno DOC

Rosso Piceno: 35–85% Montepulciano + 15–50% Sangiovese; Rosso Piceno Sangiovese: 85–100% Sangiovese; Rosso Piceno Superiore: a smaller sub-zone in the south-east corner, lower max. yields, higher min. ABV, not released before 1 November of the year after harvest.
slides.8.title: 📚 Verdicchio's Ageing Potential
slides.8.content:
🍾 Not just a young, easy-drinking white

Verdicchio is called "one of Italy's most age-worthy whites"; top Riserva can age 10–20 years.

⏳ 1–3 years

Style: fresh, fruit-led

Flavours: lemon, green apple, white flowers, almond

Acidity: pronounced, fresh

⏳ 4–7 years

Style: developing complexity

Flavours: honey, nuts, dried flowers, growing minerality

Acidity: well integrated

⏳ 8–20 years

Style: complex, elegant, deep

Flavours: petrol (like Riesling), honey, dried fruit, minerals

Note: only top Riserva reaches this stage
slides.9.title: 🍇 Other Notable Grapes
slides.9.content:
⚪ Pecorino

Native to south-western Marche and saved from extinction by Cocci Grifoni (the name comes from the Italian pecora, "sheep")

Style: aromatic, fruity, full-bodied

Flavours: white peach, apricot, citrus, white flowers, herbs

Hallmark: high sugar balanced by high acidity — rich yet fresh

⚪ Passerina

An ancient grape native to the central Adriatic coast (especially Offida)

Style: fresh, floral, mineral

Flavours: white flowers, citrus, almond, minerals

Hallmark: mineral and high in acidity; made still, passito and sparkling

🔴 Lacrima di Morro d'Alba DOC

"Lacrima" means teardrop; native to the area around Morro d’Alba

Style: intensely aromatic, bursting with fruit, light to medium body

Flavours: violet, rose, black cherry, raspberry, spice

Hallmark: one of Italy's most aromatic red grapes
slides.10.title: 🍇 Marche's Must-Know Grapes (IWS Official Material)
slides.10.content:
🔴 Red grapes

Sangiovese

Marche's most widely planted grape, mostly in the north; plantings are gradually giving way to Montepulciano, with which it is often blended.

Montepulciano

One of Italy's most widely planted varieties; needs a warm climate to ripen fully; full-bodied, high in alcohol, with pronounced tannins.

Lacrima

"Lacrima" means teardrop; native to the area around the town of Morro d’Alba; deep purple, with intense aromas of roses and violets.

Vernaccia Nera

Possibly native to Serrapetrona; a biotype of Cannonau (Garnacha), unrelated to other Vernaccias, and planted only around Serrapetrona.

⚪ White grapes

Verdicchio

Marche's signature grape, genetically identical to Veneto's Trebbiano di Soave and Turbiana — so it is not native to Marche; high in acidity, complex and age-worthy.

Pecorino

Named after the Italian pecora (sheep); native to south-western Marche and saved from extinction by Cocci Grifoni; high sugar balanced by high acidity.

Passerina

An ancient variety native to the central Adriatic coast (especially Offida); floral, citrus and tropical aromas, mineral and high in acidity; made still, passito and sparkling.

Other whites

Biancame (Bianchello del Metauro DOC), Maceratino (aka Ribona), Trebbiano Toscano, Malvasia Bianca di Candia.

slides.11.content:
🌊 Adriatic seafood

Facing the Adriatic, Marche is famous for fresh seafood, and brodetto (Marche fish stew) is its signature dish.

Verdicchio pairings

  • 🐟 Brodetto (Marche fish stew)
  • 🦐 Fritto misto (fried seafood)
  • 🍝 Spaghetti alle vongole (clam spaghetti)
  • 🧀 Pecorino sheep's cheese
  • 🍗 White meat and chicken dishes

Rosso Conero pairings

  • 🥩 Grilled red meat
  • 🍖 Porchetta (Italian roast pork)
  • 🍝 Pasta with meat sauce
  • 🧀 Aged cheeses
  • 🍄 Wild mushroom dishes

Lacrima di Morro d'Alba pairings

  • 🥗 Salads
  • 🐟 Grilled fish
  • 🍗 Spiced chicken
  • 🧀 Fresh cheeses
  • 🌿 Herb-based dishes
slides.12.title: 🏛️ History and Cultural Heritage
slides.12.content:
The name "Marche" comes from the medieval marca (border territory) — from the ancient Piceni, through Rome, the Papal States and share-cropping, to the modern rise of Verdicchio.

🏺

Antiquity: the Piceni and Rome

Period: from the 9th century BC

The Piceni settled here, giving their name to appellations such as Rosso Piceno and Piceno

Part of the Roman world from the 3rd century BC

🏰

Middle Ages: border territories

Period: 10th–16th centuries

The Holy Roman Empire created several marca border territories here (Marca di Ancona, Marca di Camerino, Marca di Fermo); the plural "Marche" became the region's name

Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II was born in Jesi in 1194

🎨

Renaissance and the Papal States

Period: 15th–19th centuries

Urbino was a great Renaissance centre (Raphael's birthplace, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site)

In 1622 Francesco Scacchi, a physician from Fabriano, published "De Salubri Potu Dissertatio", one of the earliest works to discuss sparkling wine

For most of this time part of the Papal States until joining Italy in 1860; the countryside long ran on mezzadria (share-cropping) and coltura promiscua (mixed cropping)

🍾

20th century: the rise of Verdicchio

1950s–60s: Fazi Battaglia's amphora-shaped bottle made Verdicchio popular

1968: Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi DOC created

1970s–80s: mass production of simple, neutral wines; quality producers rose in the 1980s and critics took notice in the 1990s

2010: the Riserva wines of Castelli di Jesi and Matelica became DOCG

🏺 The story of the amphora bottle

In the 1950s, Fazi Battaglia launched a curvy bottle inspired by the ancient two-handled amphora, making Verdicchio hugely popular in Italy and abroad.

The shape made Verdicchio one of the most recognisable Italian whites, but it also became tied to the cheap, mass-produced image of the 1970s–80s; today top wines mostly use standard bottles.

Inspiration

The ancient two-handled amphora

Significance

Verdicchio's first wave of international fame

Legacy

Some producers still keep the shape as a brand signature

📍 Historic towns

Jesi

Heart of Castelli di Jesi, with intact medieval walls

Birthplace of Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II (1194)

Matelica

An inland Apennine town at the heart of Verdicchio di Matelica

In Marche's only north–south valley

Urbino

Raphael's birthplace and a centre of Renaissance art

A UNESCO World Heritage Site

Ancona

The regional capital and main Adriatic port

Gateway to the Monte Cònero red-wine zone
slides.13.title: 🌄 Terroir in Depth
slides.13.content:
Marche's terroir stretches from the Adriatic coast to the Apennines; differences in altitude, climate and soil give Verdicchio two distinct expressions.

📊 Castelli di Jesi vs Matelica

FactorCastelli di JesiMatelica
🗺️ LocationHills between the Adriatic and the Apennines, in the Misa and Esino valleysInland, in Marche's only north–south valley, south-west of Jesi
⛰️ Elevation150–400 m250–500 m (higher)
🌡️ ClimateMediterranean, moderated by the seaContinental, wide day–night swings
☀️ Diurnal rangeSmallerMuch larger
📍 MGAs99; Classico sub-zone (crossed by the Esino)13; no Classico sub-zone
🪨 SoilsClay, limestone, marine sedimentsLimestone, marl, gravel
💨 MicroclimateSea breezes bring moist airValley winds create cold-air pooling
🍇 Wine styleFresh, mineral, fruit-ledStructured, high acidity, more concentrated
⏳ Ageing potential5–10 years10–20 years
🌊

The Adriatic's influence

Castelli di Jesi is moderated by the Adriatic:

  • Smaller temperature swings, steady ripening
  • Sea breezes bring minerality and a saline touch
  • Higher humidity, so disease needs watching
  • Moderate acidity, fresh fruit
🏔️

The Apennines' influence

Matelica is an inland valley sheltered by mountains:

  • Wide day–night swings keep acidity higher
  • Cold-air pooling lengthens ripening
  • More gravelly soils, excellent drainage
  • More concentrated flavour, greater ageing potential

🔑 Why is Matelica more intense?

1. Altitude and diurnal range

Higher altitude + wider day–night swings → higher acidity, more focused aromas

2. Valley microclimate

Cold-air pooling lengthens ripening → fuller phenolic development

3. Soil drainage

Gravelly limestone → deep roots, concentrated flavour

4. Low yields

More boutique management → lower yields per hectare, higher quality
slides.14.title: 🍇 Verdicchio in Depth
slides.14.content:
Verdicchio is Italy's most underrated white grape; DNA research has revealed its link to Veneto, and its biology gives it ageing potential.

🧬 DNA research and origins

DNA research (IWS materials) shows that:

  • Verdicchio is genetically identical to Veneto's Trebbiano di Soave and Turbiana (Lugana)
  • It is therefore not native to Marche, but was brought in and took root here
  • Still, Marche is its most important home and it is recognised as the region's signature grape
  • The name comes from verde (green), for the greenish tint of its skin
🧬 One grape, different names

Marche: Verdicchio; Soave: Trebbiano di Soave; Lugana: Turbiana

🍇 Style

High acidity, complex and age-worthy; almond, citrus and green apple when young

🌿 Biology and the science of ageing

🍇 The grape

  • Late-ripening: harvested late September to early October
  • Thick skin: rich in phenolics, a stable structure
  • High acidity: naturally high in tartaric acid
  • Compact bunches: need thinning to avoid disease
  • Yield: 80–100 hl/ha (lower is better)

🧪 Composition

  • Acidity: 6–8 g/L (higher than most whites)
  • Phenolics: thick skins add structure
  • Aroma precursors: rich in terpenes
  • Minerals: high in potassium and calcium

✂️ Common training systems in Marche

  • Cordone speronato: single spur-pruned cordon
  • Doppio capovolto: a Guyot variant with two canes bent downward
  • Tendone: a high overhead pergola, formerly used for high yields

🧬 The science: why can Verdicchio age so long?

1️⃣ Acidity as a preservative

Verdicchio is high in tartaric acid (6–8 g/L); acidity is a natural preservative that protects the wine from oxidation.

🔬 Principle: low pH inhibits bacteria and slows oxidation

2️⃣ The buffering effect of phenolics

Phenolic compounds from the thick skins gradually polymerise with age, building a more complex flavour structure.

🔬 Principle: phenolic polymerisation creates new aroma molecules (almond, honey)

3️⃣ Reductive ageing

Ageing sur lie creates a reductive environment that protects the wine while adding complexity to the palate.

🔬 Principle: yeast autolysis releases polysaccharides that add body

🌈 Flavour evolution: from lemon to petrol

1–3 years
🍋

Youth

Lemon, green apple, white flowers, almond

→
4–7 years
🌰

Maturity

Almond paste, honey, dried flowers, toasted hazelnut

→
8–15 years
🍯

Complexity

Honey, beeswax, dried apricot, minerals

→
15–20 years
⛽

Peak age

Petrol, truffle, dried citrus peel, amber

🛢️ The science of petrol notes

As with German Riesling, the "petrol" note of aged Verdicchio comes from the compound TDN (1,1,6-trimethyl-1,2-dihydronaphthalene), formed as carotenoids break down in an acidic environment — a hallmark of fine aged whites.
slides.15.title: 🍾 The Evolution of Winemaking
slides.15.content:
Verdicchio winemaking evolved from 1950s mass production to a modern fine-wine style, with different tiers matching different methods.

⚙️ Traditional vs modern

🏺 Traditional winemaking (1950s–1990s)

  • Harvest: machine-picked, high yields (100+ hl/ha)
  • Fermentation: stainless steel at 16–18°C
  • Ageing: almost none, bottled early
  • Style: light, simple, easy-drinking
  • Typical wine: the everyday wine of the amphora-bottle era

🔬 Modern fine winemaking (2000s–today)

  • Harvest: hand-picked, controlled yields (50–70 hl/ha)
  • Fermentation: stainless steel plus some oak
  • Sur lie: 6–18 months on the lees
  • Oak: French oak ageing (Riserva)
  • Style: complex, structured, age-worthy
  • Typical wine: Riserva, single-vineyard Classico

🍷 Three style tiers

Entry

Verdicchio DOC

Winemaking: stainless steel, little or no ageing

Flavours: lemon, green apple, white flowers, fresh

Alcohol: 11.5–12%

Ageing potential: 1–3 years

Occasion: everyday drinking, with seafood

Examples:
  • Fazi Battaglia Verdicchio DOC
  • Garofoli Macrina
  • Umani Ronchi Verdicchio
Mid

Classico Superiore / Riserva DOCG

Winemaking: 6–12 months sur lie, some oak

Flavours: white peach, almond, honey, minerals

Alcohol: 12.5–13%

Ageing potential: 5–10 years

Occasion: special meals, short-term cellaring

Examples:
  • Sartarelli Tralivio
  • Bucci Villa Bucci Riserva
  • Garofoli Serra Fiorese
Top

Single vineyard / top Riserva

Winemaking: hand-picked, barrel-fermented and aged 18–24 months

Flavours: honey, toasted hazelnut, petrol, truffle, minerals

Alcohol: 13–13.5%

Ageing potential: 10–20 years

Occasion: cellaring, celebrations

Examples:
  • Bucci Pongelli Riserva (single vineyard)
  • Bisci Vigneto Fogliano
  • Sartarelli Balciana (old vines)

🔧 Special techniques

Sur lie (lees ageing)

Ageing the wine on dead yeast cells, whose autolysis releases:

  • Polysaccharides: a rounder body
  • Glycerol: a smoother palate
  • Complex aromas: toast, butter, yeast

⏱️ Usually 6–18 months, with regular stirring (bâtonnage)

Use of oak

Riserva wines often use French oak (225–500 L):

  • New oak: 0–20% (to avoid overt oakiness)
  • Used barrels: 2–5 years old, gentle micro-oxygenation
  • Effect: more structure, vanilla and toasted hazelnut

🪵 Usually Allier or Tronçais oak

Spumante (sparkling)

Verdicchio also makes good sparkling wine:

  • Charmat method: second fermentation in tank, fresh and fruity
  • Traditional method: second fermentation in bottle, complex yeasty notes
  • Style: dry (Brut), high acidity

🍾 About 5% of the market, but excellent quality
slides.16.title: 🏔️ Conero and Montepulciano
slides.16.content:
Monte Conero is a limestone massif on the Adriatic coast, and its Montepulciano is quite different in style from Abruzzo's.

🗻 Monte Conero's geography

📍 Location

South of Ancona, a standalone massif on the Adriatic coast

Highest point: 572 m (Monte Conero)

Climate: warmer south of Cònero, helping Montepulciano ripen fully

🌡️ Microclimate

Sea influence: mild climate, summers not too hot

Sea breezes: bring cool air and minerality

Plenty of sun: south-facing slopes help Montepulciano ripen

🪨 Soils

Limestone base: Cretaceous marine sediments

Red clay: iron-rich, adds structure

Good drainage: sloping terrain avoids waterlogging

🍇 Montepulciano: Marche vs Abruzzo

FeatureMarche (Conero)Abruzzo
🌍 SettingA limestone promontory on the Adriatic coastBroad hills from the Adriatic coast inland
🍷 StyleDark, robust, full-bodied (Riserva)Rich fruit, supple, easy-drinking
🌸 AromasBlack cherry, plum, spice, leatherBlack cherry, plum, spice, chocolate
🏗️ StructurePronounced tannins, high alcohol, full bodyModerate acidity, supple tannins, round
⏳ Ageing5–15 years (Riserva)3–8 years

📜 Rosso Cònero DOC vs Cònero DOCG

Rosso Cònero DOC

  • Grapes: min. 85% Montepulciano, Sangiovese allowed
  • Style: lighter, fruit-forward, approachable
  • Positioning: the entry to Cònero reds

Cònero DOCG (Riserva)

  • Grapes: min. 85% Montepulciano (max. 15% Sangiovese); most producers use 100% Montepulciano
  • Ageing: min. 2 years
  • Status: DOCG since 2004
  • Style: dark, robust, full-bodied, tannic, high in alcohol

⏳ How Conero ages

1–3 years

Youth

Flavours: red cherry, plum, violet, fresh spice

Tannins: noticeable but supple

Palate: fruit-led, lively

4–8 years

Maturity

Flavours: cherry jam, dried flowers, leather, tobacco

Tannins: well integrated, silky

Palate: balanced, complex

9–15 years

Full maturity

Flavours: dried fruit, truffle, forest floor, spice box

Tannins: fully melded, elegant

Palate: deep, layered

🍽️ Conero food pairing

🐖 Porchetta (Italian roast pork)

A Marche classic: herb-stuffed pork belly roll roasted until crisp:

  • Conero's acidity cuts the richness
  • Herbal notes echo rosemary and sage
  • Tannins are a perfect match for the crackling

🍷 Recommended: Conero Riserva (5–8 years old)

Other pairings:
  • 🥩 Chargrilled steak, lamb chops
  • 🍝 Pappardelle with wild boar ragù (pappardelle al cinghiale)
  • 🧀 Aged Pecorino sheep's cheese
  • 🍄 Truffle dishes
slides.17.title: 🌸 Three Emerging Grapes
slides.17.content:
Beyond Verdicchio, Marche has revived three traditional grapes in recent years, each with its own personality and market potential.

🐑

Pecorino

The "sheep grape" — a white revival star

📛 Name

From the Italian pecora (sheep), because sheep love to eat these grapes; medieval shepherds noticed their flocks picking them out, hence the name.

🌱 The revival

20th century: nearly extinct, kept only by a few old farmers

1980s: Guido Cocci Grifoni tracked down old vines and led the revival

2001 / 2011: Offida DOC created, elevated to DOCG in 2011 (Offida Pecorino)

Today: plantings have grown to 500+ ha

🍇 Grape traits

  • Early-ripening: picked in early September
  • High sugar + high acidity: rich yet fresh
  • Intensely aromatic: rich in terpenes
  • Full-bodied: rounder than Verdicchio

🌈 Flavour profile

Nose: white peach, apricot, tropical fruit, white flowers, herbs

Palate: full, round, mineral

Finish: almond, citrus peel, sea salt

🐦

Passerina

The "sparrow grape" — a rising sparkling star

📛 Name

From the Italian passero (sparrow), because sparrows love to peck at these grapes; the tight bunches attract birds, and growers named it accordingly.

🌱 Tradition and today

Traditionally: used for simple everyday whites

2000s: quality producers discovered its sparkling potential

Today: recognised in Offida DOCG, made both still and sparkling

🍇 Grape traits

  • Mid-early ripening: picked in mid-September
  • High acidity: ideal for sparkling wine
  • Floral: white flowers, honeysuckle
  • Fresh style: similar to Pinot Grigio

🌈 Flavour profile

Nose: white flowers, citrus, green apple, almond, minerals

Palate: fresh, medium-bodied, strongly mineral

Finish: white flowers, almond, sea breeze

🍾 Sparkling style

Offida Passerina Spumante: Charmat or traditional method

Fresh, floral, high acidity — an ideal aperitif

💧

Lacrima di Morro d'Alba

The "teardrop" — an aromatic red bombshell

📛 Name

Lacrima means "tear", because the thin skins let juice seep out like teardrops. Morro d'Alba is the zone (a village near Ancona).

🌱 Back from the brink

20th century: almost extinct

1985: Lacrima di Morro d’Alba DOC created and conservation began

Today: about 100–150 ha, a boutique niche

🍇 Grape traits

  • Early-ripening: picked in early September
  • Thin-skinned and juicy: oxidises easily, must be handled quickly
  • Extremely aromatic: very high in terpenes
  • Low tannin: best drunk young

🌈 Flavour profile (Italy's most aromatic red)

Nose: 🌸 violet, rose, black cherry, raspberry, cinnamon

Palate: light to medium body, supple tannins, bursting fruit

Finish: flowers, berries, spice

🍷 Styles

Young and easy: stainless-steel fermentation to keep the florals

Superiore: richer and fuller-bodied; there is also a Passito

📊 The three grapes compared

FeaturePecorino 🐑Passerina 🐦Lacrima 💧
ColourWhiteWhiteRed

AcidityHighHighMedium
BodyFullLightLight to medium
Main aromasWhite peach, apricotWhite flowers, citrusViolet, rose
Plantings500+ ha300+ ha100–150 ha

slides.19.title: 🏰 Producers and Buying Guide
slides.19.content:
Marche has a fine group of producers, from century-old traditions to modern innovators, with wines at every level for every need.

🍾 15+ top Verdicchio producers

S tier

Bucci

The spiritual leader of Castelli di Jesi, organically farmed

Flagships:
  • Villa Bucci Riserva — ages 15–20 years
  • Pongelli Riserva — single vineyard, top of the range

🌟 Highlights: old-vine Verdicchio, organic farming, depth and elegance

S tier

Sartarelli

A 100% Verdicchio specialist and benchmark of Castelli di Jesi

Flagships:
  • Tralivio — classic Riserva
  • Balciana — old-vine single vineyard

🌟 Highlights: family-run, Verdicchio only, consistent quality

S tier

Bisci

King of Matelica, with the greatest ageing potential

Flagships:
  • Vigneto Fogliano — single vineyard
  • Verdicchio di Matelica Riserva

🌟 Highlights: high altitude, old vines, ages 20+ years

A tier

Umani Ronchi

Marche's largest quality estate, strong in both Verdicchio and Conero

Recommended:
  • Casal di Serra Verdicchio
  • Plenio Verdicchio Riserva
A tier

Garofoli

Founded in 1871, balancing tradition and innovation

Recommended:
  • Podium Verdicchio Riserva
  • Serra Fiorese Riserva
A tier

Fazi Battaglia

Behind the amphora-shaped bottle, the force that took Verdicchio international

Recommended:
  • Le Mole Riserva
  • San Sisto Riserva
Other quality Verdicchio producers:
MoncaroMarotti CampiColonnaraPievaltaAndrea FeliciSparapaniBonciSanta BarbaraTavignano

🍷 Top Conero red producers

S tier

Umani Ronchi - Cumaro

The benchmark Conero, 100% Montepulciano

🍷 18 months in French oak, ages 10–15 years

S tier

Moroder

Small-production boutique Conero, organically farmed

🍷 Traditional style, elegant and refined

A tier

Lanari

Family-run, excellent value

A tier

Le Terrazze

Small batches, old-vine Montepulciano

🌸 Producers of the emerging grapes

Cocci Grifoni

The saviour of Pecorino, an Offida pioneer

Pecorino: Guido Cocci Grifoni rescued Pecorino from old vines in the 1980s

Velenosi

A leading Offida estate, strong in both Pecorino and Lacrima

Pecorino: Velenosi Pecorino

Lacrima: Lacrima di Morro d'Alba

Aurora

A new-generation estate, organically farmed

Pecorino: Aurora Pecorino

Passerina: Spumante

Oasi degli Angeli

A cult Montepulciano estate with a boutique focus

Kurni: a top 100% Montepulciano red

🛒 Buying guide by tier

Entry

For: everyday drinking, a first taste of Marche

Picks

  • Umani Ronchi Verdicchio DOC
  • Garofoli Macrina Verdicchio
  • Fazi Battaglia Anfora
  • Lanari Rosso Conero

Mid

For: special meals, short-term cellaring

Picks

  • Sartarelli Tralivio Riserva
  • Bucci Villa Bucci Riserva
  • Garofoli Podium Riserva
  • Umani Ronchi Plenio
  • Velenosi Pecorino

Top

For: long-term cellaring, celebrations

Picks

  • Bucci Pongelli Riserva
  • Sartarelli Balciana
  • Bisci Vigneto Fogliano
  • Umani Ronchi Cumaro

📦 Cellaring advice

🍾 Verdicchio to cellar

  • Must-have: Matelica Riserva (10–20 years)
  • Recommended: Castelli di Jesi Classico Riserva (5–15 years)
  • Skip: regular DOC (drink young)

🌡️ Storage: 12–15°C, 70% humidity, away from light

🍷 Conero to cellar

  • Conero Riserva DOCG (5–15 years)
  • Top single vineyards (10–15 years)

📅 When to buy and drink

Buy: on release of a new vintage (lower prices)

Drink

  • Verdicchio Riserva: peaks after 5–7 years
  • Conero Riserva: peaks after 6–10 years
slides.20.title: ⚖️ The Two Great Verdicchio Zones Compared
slides.20.description: Marche's two great Verdicchio zones are only 60 km apart, yet sea and mountains make them completely different: Castelli di Jesi is softened by sea breezes, Matelica is bracing mountain-valley country.
slides.20.pairs.0.title: Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi vs di Matelica — sea and mountain
slides.20.pairs.0.intro: Marche's two great Verdicchio zones are only 60 km apart, yet sea and mountains make them completely different: Castelli di Jesi is softened by sea breezes, Matelica is bracing mountain-valley country.
slides.20.pairs.0.left.name: Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi DOC
slides.20.pairs.0.left.ageing: None for the basic wine; Riserva 18 months (DOCG)
slides.20.pairs.0.left.style: Softer, bright fruit, moderate minerality, for earlier drinking
slides.20.pairs.0.left.aromas: Green apple, lemon, white flowers, almond, a saline touch (sea breeze)
slides.20.pairs.0.right.name: Verdicchio di Matelica DOC
slides.20.pairs.0.right.climate: Continental valley climate, wide day–night swings, no sea influence
slides.20.pairs.0.right.ageing: None for the basic wine; Riserva 18 months
slides.20.pairs.0.right.style: Lean and taut, very high acidity, strong mineral tension, excellent ageing potential
slides.20.pairs.0.right.aromas: Lime, white flowers, flint, smoke, white pepper, nuts (with age)
slides.20.pairs.0.right.producers: Belisario, La Monacesca, Bisci, Borgo Paglianetto
slides.20.pairs.0.keyDifference: Sea breezes give Castelli di Jesi soft fruit and a light saline touch; the Matelica valley has no sea breeze and wide day–night swings, producing very high acidity and mineral depth. Though tiny (about a tenth of Castelli di Jesi's output), Matelica ages better — after 5–15 years it can develop remarkable complexity.
slides.21.title: 🎓 Key Takeaways
slides.21.points.0: ✓ Marche is famous for Verdicchio, yet it grows more red grapes than white; Sangiovese is the most planted, and about 20% of vineyards are organic
slides.21.points.1: ✓ 5 DOCGs: Castelli di Jesi Verdicchio Riserva, Verdicchio di Matelica Riserva, Cònero, Vernaccia di Serrapetrona, Offida
slides.21.points.2: ✓ Verdicchio is genetically identical to Veneto's Trebbiano di Soave (not native to Marche) — high in acidity, complex, age-worthy
slides.21.points.3: ✓ Castelli di Jesi (between the Misa and Esino, 99 MGAs, with a Classico zone) vs Matelica (inland north–south valley, 13 MGAs, no Classico); both Riserva DOCGs need 18 months of ageing
slides.21.points.4: ✓ Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi DOC is Marche's largest appellation by area and production; Fazi Battaglia's amphora bottle made it famous in the 1950s–60s
slides.21.points.5: ✓ Cònero DOCG (Riserva): min. 85% Montepulciano, min. 2 years, dark and robust; Rosso Cònero DOC is lighter
slides.21.points.6: ✓ Rosso Piceno: 35–85% Montepulciano + 15–50% Sangiovese; the Superiore comes only from the south-east sub-zone
slides.21.points.7: ✓ Vernaccia di Serrapetrona DOCG is Italy's only DOCG making only red sparkling wine (at least 40% dried grapes, three fermentations)
slides.21.points.8: ✓ Offida DOCG: Pecorino (saved by Cocci Grifoni), Passerina, and Rosso (Montepulciano, Cabernet Sauvignon allowed)
slides.21.points.9: ✓ Lacrima di Morro d’Alba is one of Italy's most aromatic red grapes (rose, violet)
slides.22.title: 🧠 Marche Knowledge Check
slides.22.questions.0.question: Of the two Verdicchio DOCGs, which has more structure and greater ageing potential?
slides.22.questions.0.explanation: Verdicchio di Matelica lies in an inland valley at higher altitude with wide day–night swings, giving wines with higher acidity, more structure and greater ageing potential.
slides.22.questions.1.question: Which grape is the basis of Cònero DOCG / Rosso Cònero DOC?
slides.22.questions.1.explanation: Both Cònero DOCG and Rosso Cònero DOC are based on at least 85% Montepulciano, with a little Sangiovese allowed; most Cònero Riserva is 100% Montepulciano.
slides.22.questions.2.question: What aroma can Verdicchio Riserva develop with age?
slides.22.questions.2.explanation: Top Verdicchio Riserva can age 10–20 years, developing honey, nuts and petrol notes, similar to aged German Riesling.
slides.22.questions.3.question: What is the most striking feature of Lacrima di Morro d'Alba?
slides.22.questions.3.explanation: Lacrima di Morro d'Alba is one of Italy's most aromatic red grapes, famous for intense violet, rose and black cherry aromas.
slides.22.questions.4.question: What is the minimum ageing for Castelli di Jesi Verdicchio Riserva DOCG?
slides.22.questions.4.explanation: IWS: both Castelli di Jesi Verdicchio Riserva DOCG and Verdicchio di Matelica Riserva DOCG require at least 18 months of ageing, often in wood.
slides.22.questions.5.question: Which of these grapes is NOT native to Marche?
slides.22.questions.5.explanation: Verdicchio is genetically identical to Veneto's Trebbiano di Soave and Turbiana, so it is not native to Marche; Passerina, Pecorino and Lacrima are all local natives.
slides.22.questions.6.question: Which statement about Vernaccia di Serrapetrona DOCG is FALSE?
slides.22.questions.6.options.0: A. It is Italy's only DOCG that makes only red sparkling wine
slides.22.questions.6.options.1: B. It is made by the Traditional Method (second fermentation in bottle)
slides.22.questions.6.options.2: C. Part of the grapes must be dried
slides.22.questions.6.options.3: D. It goes through three fermentations
slides.22.questions.6.explanation: Vernaccia di Serrapetrona DOCG requires at least 40% of the grapes to be dried and three fermentations, but it is not made by the Traditional Method (second fermentation in bottle).
slides.22.questions.7.question: Which grapes are allowed in Offida Rosso DOCG?
slides.22.questions.7.explanation: Offida Rosso DOCG is based on at least 85% Montepulciano, with Cabernet Sauvignon allowed as a partner; it needs at least 24 months of ageing (12 in wood, 3 in bottle).
slides.22.questions.8.question: Which statement about the Matelica zone is FALSE?
slides.22.questions.8.options.1: B. Its climate is more continental and cooler than Castelli di Jesi
slides.22.questions.8.options.2: C. It lies in a valley running east–west
slides.22.questions.8.options.3: D. It lies south-west of Castelli di Jesi
slides.22.questions.8.explanation: Matelica lies in Marche's only north–south valley (parallel to the coast); most other Marche valleys run east–west, perpendicular to the coast.
slides.22.questions.9.question: Which producer made Verdicchio popular with an amphora-shaped bottle?
slides.22.questions.9.explanation: In the 1950s–60s Fazi Battaglia made Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi hugely popular with its amphora-shaped bottle.
